value: My name is William. I was born in Texas in Houston, although we moved to Austin before I can remember anything. I grew up on the south side of town, a block away from my elementry school, William's Elementary. Yes really. Growing up I was fond of D&D, which evolved into a love for playing games on computers that were similar in genre. That, in turn, gave birth to my plan to be a designer. About the time I would have started that career the personal computer had become all but common place and I found the internet a year or two before it started to become more common. Having started with computers and the internet early on grew to a career where I've always had an advantaged because I was born with the right neurodivergence at the right time

value: There is a place near Snoqualmie that's right off the highway, down one of the numerous side roads in the middle of nowhere. It seemed like it had been a maintained campground for large groups once upon a time except there wasn't more than the one large spot. You would have to drive down this dirt "road" that was perilous for trucks and dangerous for smaller cars that would lead directly to a loop that had two or three smaller spots and a massive central area. All of it cleared out of trees and any major debris, and after every winter somebody would come clear out downed trees and other obstructions. We went out there more times than I can remember, as home base for weeks we would do multiple hikes or a long weekend with large groups where we'd spend the night with a large fire and questionable substances. We got older, people moved away, and I can't think of reason I'd ever go back there now that I'm old and grey. It was a place that promised adventure, or a good time the second you turned on that unassuming side road to get there.

value: He was tired. The anxiety, insomnia, and the panic attacks that were all but behind him had taken their toll. His son not 50 feet away from him, staring at his phone and mumbling to himself. His wife in a home office not more than 100 ft from him arranging the release of several employees at her company. The time away from his own job combined with the beginning of what would be 8 wees of therapy increasing the weight of feeling useless in every way. His family ambivalent, not just because they were engaged now, but all the time. It was then that he made a decision that would change everything.
